Power unit: Overcurrent
meaning: The Motor Module's power stage measured current above its hardware limit and switched the output off to protect the IGBTs.
symptoms: Trips the moment the axis is enabled or while accelerating; can also trip at random under heavy load.
causes: Short or ground fault in the motor cable or motor winding; failed IGBT, gate driver or current sensor in the power unit; wrong motor data or over-aggressive current/speed controller settings; motor cable too long.
checks: With power isolated and the DC link discharged, megger the motor and cable phase to ground; compare the winding resistance of all three phases; if motor and cable test good, the power unit is the likely cause.
repairable: Yes: power stage faults (IGBT, gate drive, current sensing) are a common repair.
service: Servo drive repair; servo motor repair

name: Power unit: DC link voltage overvoltage
meaning: The DC link (DC bus) voltage rose above the trip level, usually because a braking motor fed energy back into the drive faster than it could be absorbed.
symptoms: Trips while the axis is slowing down, on fast stops, or when a vertical axis is lowered.
causes: Deceleration ramp too short for the load inertia; braking resistor, Braking Module or regenerative infeed not working; supply voltage too high or spiking; DC link voltage controller switched off.
checks: Note whether the trip always happens during braking; check the braking resistor's resistance and wiring; measure the incoming line voltage.
repairable: Often a setting or braking-circuit issue; repairable when the infeed or the drive's voltage sensing is faulty.
service: Servo drive repair; infeed (Line Module) repair

name: Power unit: DC link voltage undervoltage
meaning: The DC link voltage dropped below the minimum the power unit needs to keep running.
symptoms: Trips on supply dips, when several axes accelerate together, or right after switch-on; other axes on the same infeed may report it too.
causes: Missing phase, blown fuse or voltage dip on the supply; Line Module (infeed) failing or not ready; loose DC link busbars; precharge or DC link capacitor problems.
checks: Measure all three supply phases under load; check the fuses; with power off, check the DC link busbar screws between modules.
repairable: Yes, when the infeed or power unit is the cause.
service: Infeed (Line Module) repair; servo drive repair

name: Power unit: Overtemperature heat sink AC inverter
meaning: The power unit's heat sink got hotter than its allowed limit.
symptoms: Trips after the machine has run for a while, more often on hot days or in long heavy cycles.
causes: Failed or clogged cooling fan; dirty heat sink or blocked airflow; cabinet too hot; drive running near or above its rating; faulty temperature sensor.
checks: Confirm the module fan is spinning; clean filters and fins; measure the cabinet temperature; compare the load current with the drive rating.
repairable: Yes: fan replacement and temperature sensor repair are routine.
service: Servo drive repair; cooling fan replacement

name: Power unit: Overload I2t
meaning: The power unit's thermal model calculated that it carried too much current for too long (I2t overload).
symptoms: Trips during long, heavy duty cycles; clears after a rest and then comes back.
causes: Mechanical binding (worn ball screw, bearings, gibs or guides); holding brake dragging; drive undersized for the duty cycle; oscillating or badly tuned control loop; motor fault drawing extra current.
checks: Compare the actual current with the module rating; with power off and the axis safely supported, feel for binding; confirm the brake releases fully.
repairable: Often mechanical; repairable when the drive's current measurement is faulty.
service: Servo drive repair; servo motor repair
